problem: The public CTAs pointed to /pakketadvies and /portaal-demo while Netlify had no explicit clean-URL rewrite for either route, so the backing HTML existed but the public routes could fail.
root_cause: The new public tool pages were added as top-level HTML files without extending the existing explicit clean-route rewrite contract in _redirects.
decision: Add explicit 200 rewrites from /pakketadvies to /pakketadvies.html and /portaal-demo to /portaal-demo.html, and treat every new top-level public CTA target as requiring route-level production readback.
prevention: Every new top-level public HTML tool must have an explicit clean-route contract when the site relies on _redirects for extensionless URLs.
CTA acceptance requires opening the production destination URL, not only checking that the backing file exists.
Public demo and advisor routes must be included in route regression coverage before promotion.
